> AGENT

Yes, root cause confirmed.

`review` reruns are correctly gated in preflight: if a scored subjective dimension still has open backlog, rerun is blocked unless `--force-review-rerun` ([preflight.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/preflight.py:236)).

The bug was in queue guidance:
- Stale subjective items with open review findings were being told to run `review --prepare --dimensions ...` instead of triaging open review findings first ([helpers.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/helpers.py:292)).
- That command then hit preflight and got blocked, creating the contradictory loop you saw.

I patched it so open review findings take priority:
- `next` now points to `desloppify show review --status open` when review findings exist, even if the dimension is stale ([helpers.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/helpers.py:294)).
- Status/subjective follow-up now also prefers `show review --status open` when issues are present ([scan_reporting_subjective.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/scan/scan_reporting_subjective.py:86)).

Regression tests added:
- [test_work_queue.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/review/test_work_queue.py:266)
- [test_scan_reporting_direct.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/scan/test_scan_reporting_direct.py:724)

Validation:
- `pytest` targeted tests passed.
- `desloppify next --count 3` now shows `Action: desloppify show review --status open`.
- `desloppify status` now shows `Next command to improve subjective scores: desloppify show review --status open`.

If you want, I can continue from here and run through the actual review queue items in order.

and blind packet snapshots for runner workflows.\"\"\"\n    return runner_packets_mod.write_packet_snapshot(\n        packet,\n        stamp=stamp,\n        review_packet_dir=review_packet_dir,\n return runner_packets_mod.build_blind_packet(packet)\n\n\ndef sha256_file(path: Path) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Compute sha256 hex digest for path contents (or None on read failure).\"\"\"\n    return runner_packets_mod.sha256_file(path)\n\n\ndef build_batch_import_provenance(\n    *,\n    runner: str,\n    blind_packet_path: Path,\n    run_stamp: str,\n    batch_indexes: list[int],\n) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Build provenance payload used to trust assessment-bearing imports.\"\"\"\n    return runner_packets_mod.build_batch_import_provenance(\n        runner=runner,\n        blind_packet_path=blind_packet_path,\n        run_stamp=run_stamp,\n        batch_indexes=batch_indexes,\n    )\n\n\ndef selected_batch_indexes(\n    *,\n    raw_selection: str | None,\n    batch_count: int,\n    parse_fn,\n    colorize_fn,\n) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Validate selected batch indexes or exit with a CLI error.\"\"\"\n    return runner_packets_mod.selected_batch_indexes(\n        raw_selection=raw_selection,\n        batch_count=batch_count,\n        parse_fn=parse_fn,\n        colorize_fn=colorize_fn,\n    )\n\n\ndef prepare_run_artifacts(\n    *,\n    stamp: str,\n    selected_indexes: list[int],\n    batches: list[dict],\n    packet_path: Path,\n    run_root: Path,\n    repo_root: Path,\n    build_prompt_fn,\n    safe_write_text_fn,\n    colorize_fn,\n) -> tuple[Path, Path, dict[int, Path], dict[int, Path], dict[int, Path]]:\n    \"\"\"Build prompt/output/log paths and persist prompts for selected batches.\"\"\"\n    return runner_packets_mod.prepare_run_artifacts(\n        stamp=stamp,\n        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,\n        batches=batches,\n        packet_path=packet_path,\n        run_root=run_root,\n        repo_root=repo_root,\n        build_prompt_fn=build_prompt_fn,\n        safe_write_text_fn=safe_write_text_fn,\n        colorize_fn=colorize_fn,\n    )\n\n\ndef execute_batches(\n    *,\n    tasks: dict[int, object],\n    run_parallel: bool,\n    progress_fn=None,\n    error_log_fn=None,\n    max_parallel_workers: int | None = None,\n    heartbeat_seconds: float | None = 15.0,\n    clock_fn,\n) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Run indexed tasks and return failed index list.\"\"\"\n    return runner_parallel_mod.execute_batches(\n        tasks=tasks,\n        run_parallel=run_parallel,\n        progress_fn=progress_fn,\n        error_log_fn=error_log_fn,\n        max_parallel_workers=max_parallel_workers,\n        heartbeat_seconds=heartbeat_seconds,\n        clock_fn=clock_fn,\n    )\n\n\ndef _extract_payload_from_log(\n    batch_index: int,\n    raw_path: Path,\n    extract_fn,\n) -> dict[str, object] | None:\n    \"\"\"Try to recover a batch payload from the runner log file.\"\"\"\n    log_path = raw_path.parent.parent / \"logs\" / f\"batch-{batch_index + 1}.log\"\n    if not log_path.exists():\n        return None\n    try:\n        log_text = log_path.read_text()\n    except OSError:\n        return None\n\n    stdout_marker = \"\\nSTDOUT:\\n\"\n    stderr_marker = \"\\n\\nSTDERR:\\n\"\n    stdout_start = log_text.rfind(stdout_marker)\n    if stdout_start == -1 and log_text.startswith(\"STDOUT:\\n\"):\n        stdout_start = 0\n        stdout_offset = len(\"STDOUT:\\n\")\n    elif stdout_start >= 0:\n        stdout_offset = len(stdout_marker)\n    else:\n        stdout_offset = 0\n    if stdout_start >= 0:\n        start_idx = stdout_start + stdout_offset\n        stdout_end = log_text.find(stderr_marker, start_idx)\n        stdout_text = (\n            log_text[start_idx:]\n            if stdout_end == -1\n            else log_text[start_idx:stdout_end]\n        )\n        payload = extract_fn(stdout_text)\n        if payload is not None:\n            return payload\n        return None\n\n    return extract_fn(log_text)\n\n\ndef collect_batch_results(\n    *,\n    selected_indexes: list[int],\n    failures: list[int],\n    output_files: dict[int, Path],\n    allowed_dims: set[str],\n    extract_payload_fn,\n    normalize_result_fn,\n) -> tuple[list[BatchResult], list[int]]:\n    \"\"\"Parse and normalize batch outputs, preserving prior failures.\"\"\"\n    batch_results: list[BatchResult] = []\n    failure_set = set(failures)\n    for idx in selected_indexes:\n        had_execution_failure = idx in failure_set\n        raw_path = output_files[idx]\n        payload = None\n        parsed_from_log = False\n        if raw_path.exists():\n            try:\n                payload = extract_payload_fn(raw_path.read_text())\n            except OSError:\n                payload = None\n        if payload is None:\n            payload = _extract_payload_from_log(idx, raw_path, %s\", exc)\n        try:\n            assessments, findings, dimension_notes, quality = normalize_result_fn(\n                payload,\n                allowed_dims,\n            )\n        except ValueError:\n            failure_set.add(idx)\n            continue\n        if had_execution_failure:\n            failure_set.discard(idx)\n        batch_results.append(\n            BatchResult(\n          )\n        )\n    return batch_results, sorted(failure_set)\n\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"BatchProgressEvent\",\n    \"BatchResult\",\n    \"CodexBatchRunnerDeps\",\n    \"FollowupScanDeps\",\n \"write_packet_snapshot\",\n]\nEOF"

Core package is the only allowed direct importer of private internals.\n+    if rel.startswith(\"desloppify/core/\"):\n+        return []\n+    try:\n+        tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(), filename=str(path))\n+    except SyntaxError:\n+        return []\n+    violations: list[str] = []\n+    for node in ast.walk(tree):\n+        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):\n+            for alias in node.names:\n+                name = alias.name\n+                if name == _PRIVATE_INTERNAL_MODULE or name.startswith(\n+                    f\"{_PRIVATE_INTERNAL_MODULE}.\"\n+                ):\n+                    violations.append(f\"{rel}:{node.lineno} import {name}\")\n+        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):\n+            module = node.module or \"\"\n+            if module == _PRIVATE_INTERNAL_MODULE or module.startswith(\n+                f\"{_PRIVATE_INTERNAL_MODULE}.\"\n+            ):\n+                violations.append(f\"{rel}:{node.lineno} from {module} import ...\")\n+                continue\n+            if module == \"desloppify.core\":\n+                for alias in node.names:\n+                    if alias.name == \"_internal\":\n+                        violations.append(\n+                            f\"{rel}:{node.lineno} from desloppify.core import _internal\"\n+                        )\n+    return violations\n+\n+\n def test_runtime_code_avoids_deprecated_compat_facades():\n@@\n     assert not violations, \"runtime imports deprecated compat facades:\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(\n         sorted(violations)\n     )\n+\n+\n+def test_non_core_runtime_code_avoids_private_internal_imports():\n+    violations: list[str] = []\n+    for path, rel in _runtime_python_files():\n+        violations.extend(_private_internal_import_violations(path, rel))\n+    assert not violations, \"runtime imports private core._internal modules:\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(\n+        sorted(violations)\n+    )\n*** End Patch\n"

Root cause is clearer: importing `review.dimensions.data` implicitly loads `review.dimensions.__init__`, which currently imports `dimensions.lang` and triggers plugin discovery during `state` import. I’m making `review.dimensions` lazy so language-plugin enumeration only happens when those specific exports are requested.
